subject.title: TUI /sessions list: gateway-injected inbound metadata block used as session title (shows 'untrusted metadata' for all sessions)

question: Should maintainers adopt the open fork PR, replace it with a fresh narrow same-repo fix, or close that branch before queueing another fix for this issue?
rationale: The bug shape is clear, but the issue has an open conflicting fork PR with closing syntax and no maintainer edit access, so automation should not create a competing fix PR until maintainers choose the branch path.

options.title: Replace With Fresh Narrow Fix
options.body: Close or supersede the stale fork branch and land a same-repo fix covering metadata stripping plus sync and async display-name hydration.

options.title: Adopt Or Rebase Fork PR
options.body: Have a maintainer or contributor update the fork PR to current main, add missing proof and coverage, then review it as the landing candidate.

options.title: Keep Waiting On Fork PR
options.body: Leave the issue blocked on the existing fork PR despite conflicts, no maintainer edit access, and no update since April 2026.

recommendation.title: Replace With Fresh Narrow Fix
recommendation.body: Close or supersede the stale fork branch and land a same-repo fix covering metadata stripping plus sync and async display-name hydration.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest recent routing signal from merged TUI/session-list and Gateway session-organization work on the affected files.
